title: /import: common spreadsheet cell shapes fail whole rows (dotted / compact dates, option value case, one error per row)
body:
Ruled: 6377844879 · batch #9 item 3a · letter A · 2026-10-24T00:43:45Z (proposals 1, 2, 4; not 3)

## Context

Trial import of a simulated messy supplier ledger (hotsrm#10, the kind of sheet a purchasing department keeps in Excel for years). These are the cell shapes that failed rows which a person reads without hesitation. Each failure rejects the whole row, including rows where the bad cell is an optional field.

| Cell | Field type | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2011.07.01` | date | `invalid_date` | 2011-07-01 (`YYYY.MM.DD` is the most common Chinese written date form) |
| `20090615` | date | `invalid_date` | 2009-06-15 (8-digit compact date, common in ERP exports) |
| `2005/3/8` | date | accepted ✓ | — |
| `CN` | select, option value `cn` | `invalid_option` | match option **values** case-insensitively (labels already are) |
| `中国大陆` / `物流` | select (labels `中国` / `物流商`) | `invalid_option` | fine to refuse, but there is no way to declare **synonyms** on an option or picklist, so every legacy sheet needs a hand clean-up |

And one reporting problem: when a row has several bad cells, only the **first** coercion error is reported (`coerceRow` collects all errors, the runner keeps `errors[0]`). The operator fixes one cell, re-runs, finds the next one. Two to three rounds per row in our trial.

## Proposal

1. Accept `YYYY.MM.DD` and `YYYYMMDD` in `parseDateCell` (unambiguous, year first).
2. Case-insensitive match on option values.
3. ~~Optional `aliases: string[]` on select options / picklist options, used by import coercion only.~~ (not in letter A — a new permanent metadata key waits for a second app; ruling 6377844879)
4. Report all cell errors of a row (e.g. `errors: [{ field, code, message }]` next to the existing first-error keys).

## Temporary measure in hotsrm

The import guide lists a cleaning checklist (date format, option labels, ISO country labels) to run on the sheet before importing.
